result.note: Tests the key parameters of the deferred UPI merchant discount rate: rate, threshold, cap and original start date.

questions.prompt: In October 2026, the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) deferred a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on Unified Payments Interface (UPI) payments until after Diwali. Consider the following statements about this fee:
items: It is levied at 0.4 percent on UPI payments to merchants above INR 2,000.
It was originally due to start on November 8, 2026.
Finance Ministry notifications capped it at INR 300 per transaction.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong: the fee was due to start on October 15, while November 8 is the date of Diwali, after which it has now been deferred. The fee rests on Finance Ministry notifications issued on September 14 and 15.
questions.source: It was due to start on October 15 under Finance Ministry notifications issued on September 14 and 15, which capped it at INR 300 (USD 3) per transaction.
